wstep: This card describes the NCHFP method for canning halved or whole plums in a boiling-water canner. [T:SLO-100]

akapity: Stem and wash the plums. [T:ACI-186]
NCHFP uses US measures: a cup holds about 237 ml. [T:ACI-195]
To can them whole, prick the skins on two sides with a fork so they do not split. [T:ACI-186]
Freestone varieties may be halved and pitted. [T:ACI-186]
Plums may be packed in water, or in very light, light or medium syrup. [T:ACI-186]
Syrup helps keep the flavor, color and shape of the fruit, but it does not prevent spoilage. [T:ACI-067]
For a very light syrup (about 10% sugar) NCHFP uses 6 1/2 cups of water and 3/4 cup of sugar for a load of 9 pint jars, or 10 1/2 cups of water and 1 1/4 cups of sugar for 7 quart jars. [T:ACI-192]
Heat the water and sugar together and bring to a boil. [T:ACI-192]
Hot pack: add the plums to water or hot syrup and boil for 2 minutes, then cover the saucepan and let it stand for 20–30 minutes. [T:ACI-187]
Fill the jars with the hot plums and cooking liquid or syrup, leaving 1/2 inch (about 1.3 cm) of headspace. [T:ACI-187]
Raw pack: pack raw plums firmly into the jars and add hot water or syrup, leaving 1/2 inch (about 1.3 cm) of headspace. [T:ACI-188]
For both packs, put on the lids and process. [T:ACI-194]
At 0–1000 ft (up to 300 m), for hot or raw pack, process pints for 20 minutes and quarts for 25. [T:ACI-075,ACI-176]
Above 1000 ft the food may spoil if the time is not increased. [T:ACI-015]
At 1001–3000 ft (above 300 m up to 900 m) process pints for 25 minutes and quarts for 30. [T:ACI-189,ACI-176]
At 3001–6000 ft (above 900 m up to 1800 m) process pints for 30 minutes and quarts for 35. [T:ACI-190,ACI-176]
Above 6000 ft (above 1800 m) process pints for 35 minutes and quarts for 40. [T:ACI-191,ACI-176]
The card converts feet to metres and rounds the limits down, towards the longer time: 1000 ft becomes 300 m, 3000 ft becomes 900 m and 6000 ft becomes 1800 m. [T:ACI-176]
Shortening the time or cooling jars in cold water can also lead to spoilage. [T:ACI-015]
NCHFP times are for US jar sizes: a pint holds about 473 ml and a quart about 946 ml. [T:ACI-174]
JarAtlas rule (NCHFP does not test metric jars): for a jar of up to 473 ml use the pint time, and for a larger jar of up to 946 ml, for example 0.5 l or 0.9 l, use the quart time. [T:ACI-175]
This NCHFP recipe gives no time for jars larger than a quart, such as 1 l, so use smaller jars. [T:ACI-175]
